target_name: Issuance Into a Doubly Confirmed Research Decline
rationale: This is a mechanical rank-average of the two best already-tested conditioners bolted onto the identical net-issuance leg, so it adds no new economic content and its outcome is largely predictable as a blend of the two parent signals (both ~-2% alpha, t≈-2.5) rather than a test of a new mechanism.

target_name: Issuance Against Lagged Research Payoff Decay
rationale: The lag has a defensible innovation-timing rationale, but it is a single-operator edit of the gen-2 signal that will push coverage below its already thin 0.042 (a 3-year trend of a 3-year MA lagged 2 years needs ~8 years of xrd history), and the conditioner remains dominated by the sales trend rather than by research productivity per se.

target_name: Issuance by Firms Buying Innovation Instead of Building It
rationale: Build-versus-buy composition scaled by the firm's own research budget is a genuinely different conditioner from the archive's goodwill-level and intangible-growth tests, though it overlaps conceptually with the gen-0 equity-financed-intangible-expansion and gen-2 goodwill signals and still carries a large tied mass at zero for R&D firms with no goodwill activity.

target_name: Issuance Against an Unmonetized Knowledge Stock
rationale: The conditioner is essentially the classic R&D-intensity (Lev–Sougiannis / Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis) anomaly with the sign reversed, and it directly contradicts the archive's strongest ratio result (financing per dollar of accumulated intangible capital, t=-4.3), which implies issuance is worst when the knowledge stock is *small*, a conflict the proposal never addresses.

target_name: Research Decay Priced Only Within Issuers
rationale: Replacing the continuous issuance leg with a participation gate is the correct decisive test of whether the intangible conditioner prices anything independent of the known net-issuance anomaly, and the centered conditioner keeps both extreme legs populated by issuers; the main risk is that the large zero mass of non-issuers bleeds into the extreme quintiles and dilutes the portfolio spread.

target_name: Issuance by Firms With an Erratic Research Commitment
rationale: Second-moment instability of the research program is a distinct economic object from the gen-1 financing-volatility test and is untried here, but VOL(xrd/sale) is strongly confounded with firm size, age and idiosyncratic volatility, so any result will need a check that it is not a repackaged vol/size effect.
